newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat determined to see self-rule deal met.
newsitem.headline: Arafat determined to see self-rule deal met.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Monday he was determined to see agreed-upon self-rule deals with Israel implemented and warned that Palestinians would not accept something imposed on them.
"We are adamant about the accurate implementation of what had been agreed upon," Arafat told reporters upon his return to Gaza from Egypt.
"No one should think that he could force the Palestinian people to accept things they cannot accept," he said without elaborating.
Arafat is facing tough negotiations with the right-wing Israeli government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on a long-overdue Israeli army pullback from most of the West Bank town of Hebron.

Israel wants to alter the accord, which calls for handing over about 80 percent of Hebron to the PLO, in order to provide more security to about 400 Jewish settlers in the rest of the town. Arafat refuses to change the accord, saying it provides ample security for the settlers.
Arafat, who is growing more frustrated after two months of negotiations, has been trying to rally Arab states to press Israel to honour peace commitments.
On Sunday Arafat held talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo on the stalled negotiations. Arafat earlier visited the United Arab Emirates and the Gulf state of Qatar.
